claim: Preprint, not peer reviewed; SSRN 5128263; year not printed.
Effective stress sigma = S - alpha Pp; alpha = 1 is Terzaghi (Eq. 1).
Biot coefficient alpha = 1 - Kfr/Kgr from drained frame and grain bulk moduli (Eq. 2).
Under Terzaghi, drained (hydrostatic) and undrained (lithostatic) burial give different compaction trends; under Biot they coincide.
quote: a drained formation following a hydrostatic burial trend and an undrained formation following a lithostatic burial trend would exhibit quite different compaction behavior if plotted against a Terzaghi effective stress

claim: Vp-VES trends are much tighter under Biot and split cleanly into smectitic and illitic populations.
A Terzaghi model calibrated in a low-pressure basin underpredicts high pressure; one calibrated in a high-pressure basin overpredicts.
quote: a conventional Terzaghi-based effective stress/pore pressure model calibrated in a low-pressure basin would tend to predict low pressures and underpredict any high-pressure sections, while a model calibrated in a high pressure basin would tend to overpredict

claim: For soft rock or very low pore pressure, Terzaghi and Biot converge (alpha near 1).
quote: for soft rocks or very low pore pressures the Terzaghi and Biot approaches will converge

claim: The Biot trend shows no dependence on formation age or burial rate.
quote: no apparent dependence on formation age

claim: Resistivity's advantage over sonic under Terzaghi calibration disappears under Biot.
quote: This benefit disappears when using a Biot-based model

claim: With measured Vs, a vertical-stress-only Biot model matches the sub-salt section regardless of distance from salt.
quote: independent of distance from the salt body

claim: Unloading, complex stress and sand-shale disequilibrium were assumed minimal, not characterised.
quote: their potential has not been fully characterized or studied here

claim: Kgr, grain density and salinity are fitted constants and may still need local calibration.
quote: Local calibration of these properties may still be required for reliable pore pressure modeling
